questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to try studying at a smaller university and improve my Spanish.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
There was a lot of confusion from Alicantes mobility office as they are not aware that Economics students follow a trimestre system. At one of the meetings I was told that there is always problems with master students of Economics as the time schedule is significantly different from the rest of the university. 
A tip, I would have liked to known was when the deadline approaches the mobility office will fix your issues for you. So you do not need to be as proactive as I was. My proactiveness caused frustration but now knowing that the mobility office would eventually fix things I would not be as worried.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The mobility office gave me a pamphlet about the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found housing through the app Idealista which is very commonly used in Southern Europe. Would definetely recommend looking through the app.
Or else you can also reach out on facebook in the group for erasmus students in Alicante, however, I have heard of several being scammed there so be alert.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Alicante is a small city so it is very easy to get to campus by either tram or bus.
It is a great city for studying as it is rather cheap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As mentioned before, the mobility office and the Economics department have very little communication between them. So I had to write a lot of emails before they did anything.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
First you have to attend the mobility office for registration that you have arrived at the university. 
Second, they give you a meeting you have to attend the meeting time they gave me could not be changed and coincided with my classes so I was forced to miss classes.
Thirdly, you have to register online. I never managed to do so as the mobility office had not registered my courses at their own website. Eventually, the mobility office did the registration for me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot. When asking for help they said they could not do anything or I should try again.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There are plenty of places for the Economics courses and you just tell the teacher that you want to attend the class. This was extremely easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress, everything will get sorted out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great professors and TAs. I am very impressed by the academic level. They are interested in knowing who you are and you can always knock on their door for questions and support. Great experience.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Difficulty was way higher than at UCPH as the QED program is preparing the students for
Ph.Ds
. We were 8 in my class and they were all very eager about studying and the field of Economics in general. Also a very non competitive environment where everybody is sharing notes and helping each other.
You should be prepared to study a lot there are high expectations from the professors that you come prepared. I was every day at the library until 18:00 at least and so was all my classmates.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
You are judged on your class participation, assignments and there are a midterm and a final exam.
Or else classes were split into practical sessions and lectures just like UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Game theory - Micro II
Macro II
Adv Macro II - forced drop as they expect you to already know matlab before taking the course. I was not expecting this.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Game theory.
The professor is great and if you like working with formal notation this is a fantastic course to take.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was unexpected that Economics department provides everything, paper, books, pencils, pens and erasers.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Not much.
You could easily spend less on food. I have just enjoyed eating well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Gym is very cheap 10 DKK per entry.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plenty, I did not take part of many of them as I preferred spending time with my classmates.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There were other erasmus students that joined kite surfing classes and other water sports. That sounded fun but did not try it out myself.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go for hikes at the nearby mountains. Views are amazing. 
There are buses and trains to many nearby cities if you have the time go check them out. 
Or else just enjoy the sun and the beach in Alicante.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy my classmates and professors were all very welcoming

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be able to speak Spanish.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be patient with the host institution.
Engage with the other students they will give you tons of tips.
Be able to speak fairly decent Spanish it will make your life way easier.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Bring proper warm clothes. It gets really cold during the night and or winter. My apartment did not have any heating so it was freezing inside during cold days.
The cold weather caught me by surprise at least.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being exposed to another type of education and getting new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academic level.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
